Prior to purchase, I did note that my old unit was spec'd at 2.0 Sones while the new unit was spec'd at 4.0 Sones. I did not notice a difference in noise after installation - suggesting the old unit had become louder while it aged. Installation was very straightforward (requiring only a slot screwdriver to slightly bend the metal for removal and installation) and the fit was perfect.

Ordered this to repair a fan in the bathroom of a rental house.  It made for an easy repair since it was a perfect swap out of just the internal fan workings. I didn't have to remove the whole housing and put in a whole new fan. Basically plug and play.  If this matches your older exhaust fan numbers I would recommend as an easy repair option.

Replaced the fan assembly that appears to have been in the ceiling since the Jurrasic Period. That old assembly said "Patent Pending" whereas the new one says "US and Foreign Patents", so that gives you an idea how old the orginal was. Even with this age difference, the new assembly was an exact fit, dropped right in (it has two small tabs that fit into slots in the housing and you just push up the other side until the tab on that side pops into its slot) and worked great. I measured the unit at about 7 1/8" aby 7 1/4", and in comparing it to the original, side-by-side, it was a dimensional match. That actual fan sound is louder, at 3.2 sones, than the original one, which states 2.0 sones on the plate. But the old one sounded like an aircraft on takeoff that was about to lose fan blades, as it had not aged gracefully. Even so, the louder sound is fine, and gives users of the bathroom extra "privacy" in that bathroon which is off the living room hallway. Considered buying just the motor/fan but opted to get the whole unit. Glad I did; it's more expensive this way, but simple to install. Recommend the unit.

The first one of these I purchased, a couple of years ago, was a perfect replacement and is pleasantly in service. Another, identical, fan in my home started rattling, so I ordered another one of these, and, it was not a perfect replacement.

First, the fan itself, I think the only the plastic part, is a bit warped. This will shorten the life (torquing it during spinning, causing hte bearings to wear faster).

Second, the body is not a perfect fit. The flat portion is a several mms off spec, being too small, and the folded sides of the metal were both a bit longer and the tabs, a bit bigger. The end result was that, as is, the fan does not lock in place on insertion, instead, being too small, it will just fall out. I bent the folded sides outward, and squished the tabs down to make them thinner and that worked. Overall, a job that should have been 5 minutes took 20, and a fan that should last 10-20 years will probably last 5-10. That said, I don't know of an alternative :(
